03:23 < MouseLRN> Filip_ hi
03:23 < Filip_> hi MouseLRN, no sleep for you ?
03:24 < Filip_> justreading the logs
03:24 < Filip_> about wirting to Casio:
03:25 < Filip_> I've had several rather long e-mail conversations with casio Japan people
03:25 < MouseLRN> and... ?
03:25 < Filip_> mainly from the business side (product manager & marketing)
03:26 < Filip_> conversation was constructive, but they wanted a business case (prove that in the long run they're going to get money out of it)
03:26 < Filip_> I also had the impression they  do not want to hurt the MS relationship (It looks like they had a very good deal , cheap OS license, from MS)
03:27 < MouseLRN> heh
03:27 < Filip_> so in the end they did not want to actively participate. I also had a couple of 'off-the-record' conversation with technical people involved in the project (working in-directly for Casio)
03:28 < Filip_> but those were not able to provide usefull info
03:28 < Filip_> BTW: they can't put PPC on the BE. 
03:29 < MouseLRN> why?
03:29 < Filip_> MS requires a number of additional capabilities for PPC (like PPC devices MUST have IrDA), microphone and a couple of others (this is marketing requirement, not technical)
03:30 < Filip_> but Casio wanted cheap entry, so that's why they took CE (CE license is very cheap compared to PPC as well), and they left out additional, less used functions like IrDA
03:31 < MouseLRN> I see
03:32 < Filip_> congrats for finding the touch reset register !
03:32 < Filip_> next hurdle is finding the correct IRQ's for touch and serial
03:33 < MouseLRN> Also I find how to do 'soft' reset (without clearing X,Y's regs)
03:33 < MouseLRN> thanks
03:34 < Filip_> is it a bitmask at 0xaa000300  ?
03:35 < MouseLRN> yes, some sequence which needed to be wrote into four different regs, started from 0xaa000300
03:41 < MouseLRN> heh, 0xaa000304 | 0x1d00, then 0xaa000304 | 0x00ff will do 'soft' reset ;-)
03:42 < MouseLRN> 0xaa000304 -> * 0xaa000304 %)
